To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the location and divisor gain of a frequency divider in a phase-locked loop circuit strongly influence both the probability of a single-event transient (SET) causing output phase displacement on the order of one operating period and the probability of a SET propagating through the loop.

(a) SETs are more easily mitigated in the stand-alone frequency divider than the PLL circuit as a whole; (b) SETs in the PLL circuit can be more effectively reduced by increasing the feedback divisor than by increasing the output divisor.

(1) the probability of a single-event transient (SET) causing a significant phase displacement in an integer-N frequency divider depends on both the location and gain (divisor value) of the frequency divider, and (2) the propagation of SETs through a closed-loop PLL is strongly dependent on the gain of the frequency dividers in the PLL feedback and output paths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding and mitigating SETs in frequency dividers and the implications of frequency divider location in PLL circuits.
the analysis of SETs in integer-N frequency-divided PLL circuits, and the implications of this analysis on PLL hardness assurance.
the effects that the gain and location of the integer-$N$ divider have on the error-rate of the PLL circuit, as well as the propagation of single-event transients through the PLL feedback loop.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the frequency divider gain is a critical parameter that can be exploited in the design of radiation-hardened frequency synthesizer circuits.
the frequency divider in PLLs should be configured external to the closed-loop.
the frequency divider in the closed-loop PLL is the most critical component in determining both the probability and magnitude of output phase errors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the location and the gain of the frequency dividers in the PLL circuit strongly influence the probability that an ion-strike will cause a phase displacement on the order of a PLL operating-period.
the frequency divider is a weak point in a PLL circuit and that the frequency divider divisor is a design parameter that can be used to reduce SET sensitivity.

, for a given circuit design, the error-rate of the PLL circuit is a strong function of the location of the frequency divider and that the propagation of transient pulses through the PLL is a strong function, as well, of the divisor of the feedback frequency divider.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SETs in frequency dividers should be considered in the design and analysis of PLLs.
the location and configuration of the frequency divider within the PLL circuit has significant implications to the SET sensitivity of the PLL and its susceptibility to ion strikes.
SETs in PLLs can be reduced by careful circuit design and that the location of the divider and its gain can significantly influence the error rate of a PLL circuit.
